# T041 draft — Temporary browser viewing on LAN or VPN

Confirmed scenario: the guest temporarily views one item on the same LAN or a VPN with existing connectivity. The guest uses a browser without Mesh Talk. For this slice, propose an online, unlocked publisher desktop and one explicitly chosen ordinary text message. Show a preview before issuing a grant. Check current export eligibility, exclude protected, recalled and expired messages, and keep unrelated metadata out of the view. Bind the grant to the selected item and issuing desktop session. End access upon recall, source expiry, lock, logout, explicit revocation or desktop restart. A temporary route failure prevents retrieval; recovery can resume only while the same grant remains valid. Use a dedicated review listener behind a configured trusted HTTPS origin. The desktop owns grant creation, read authorization and revocation. An operator-configured narrow reverse proxy can supply HTTPS. Tailscale Serve is one candidate on an already enabled tailnet; a LAN or other VPN requires a reachable hostname with a certificate already trusted by the guest browser, for example via existing managed internal DNS and TLS. Validate each separately from a second device. Do not reuse the local agent listener or store chat keys in the proxy. See https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailscale-serve and https://www.w3.org/TR/secure-contexts/.

Propose short-lived link-only grants for the first viewing slice, with an explicit UI explanation that the link can be forwarded. Network reachability and the per-item grant both apply. Avoid caching content or logging link credentials. Define the duration and whether link plus code is needed before selecting the T042 production scope. Additional codes cannot repair a missing route or untrusted HTTPS origin.

## Evidence required for T042

Use two physical devices. On both supported LAN and VPN paths, record reachability, browser trust and successful rendering of exactly one item. Check unreachable route, untrusted origin, protected source, wrong or expired grant, recall, explicit revoke, lock/logout, sleep/wake, and app restart.
